sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose of the routing module
sections.what: Explains that this file decides which model and how much thinking each agent receives, based on how defensible its output must be. Users do not see it directly, but it sets the cost and quality of every agent's output.
sections.why: The docstring says tiers reflect how hard finance teams will push on the output, and that per-agent output limits prevent avoidable cost.
sections.watch_out: Changing a tier here changes cost and quality for every agent on that tier at once.

sections.name: ModelTier
sections.title: Three quality tiers and their models
sections.what: Defines three tiers, sketch, standard and defensible, and pins one model ID and one thinking effort to each. The model IDs are fixed strings.
sections.why: Pinning means each result can be traced to an exact model. The docstring says effort is raised only where measurement showed it helped.
sections.watch_out: If a model is retired or renamed, the agents on that tier will fail or drift, and no check in this file catches it.

sections.name: model_for
sections.title: Look up the model for a tier
sections.what: Returns the exact model ID for a tier. Agents use this so they never type model names themselves.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file description. Likely reason: one lookup means each pinned ID is changed in one place.
sections.watch_out: An unrecognised tier causes a plain lookup failure with no friendly message.

sections.name: effort_for
sections.title: Look up thinking effort for a tier
sections.what: Returns the thinking depth, low, medium or high, for a tier. Agents use it so the amount of reasoning matches the tier.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond a note that effort is raised only where measurement shows headroom.
sections.watch_out: An unrecognised tier fails with the same plain lookup error as the model lookup.

summary: Maps each agent's quality tier to a pinned AI model, a thinking depth and an output size limit, so model choices are consistent across the system.
purpose: Decides which AI model and how much thinking each agent gets, so cost and quality are chosen in one place.
why: The docstring says output that finance teams test hardest should get the most capable model. Pinned model IDs let a re-run be explained later.
how: Three tiers are defined. Each tier is mapped to one model ID and one effort level. Two lookup helpers return the model ID or effort for a tier, and agents call those helpers.
inputs: A tier value: sketch, standard or defensible.
outputs: A model ID string or an effort string.
risks: A retired or renamed model ID silently changes results and cost. Changing a tier here changes every agent using it. Output size limits are set in each agent, not here.
debug: If an agent fails with a lookup error, check that it passes a valid tier. If results drift between runs, check the pinned model IDs. The docstring refers to a run manifest that does not appear in this file.
